newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may raise wheat intervention purchase.
newsitem.headline: Poland may raise wheat intervention purchase.

text.p: The Polish government is likely to clear a plan on Tuesday to increase state intervention grain purchases on the domestic market by 200,000 tonnes of bread wheat, the government spokeswoman said.
"The government will discuss an additional purchase by the Farm Market Agency (ARR) of 200,000 tonnes of consumption wheat," Aleksandra Jakubowska told reporters on Monday.
She said the purchase would be designed to help farmers, who find it unprofitable to sell their grain because storage facilities are full after substantial imports last year and early in 1997.
Under an earlier plan, ARR was to buy 487,800 tonnes of wheat this year, of which 180,000 tonnes would be imported, and 52,500 tonnes of rye.
